overview.description: Modern Aramean cuisine is a living family and community practice. Recipes vary among Syriac, Assyrian, Chaldean, Mandaic, and other communities and across homeland and diaspora settings; no single menu represents every Aramean household.

staple_dishes.name: Mujadra
staple_dishes.description: Lentils cooked with bulgur or rice and onions. Families prepare it in different ways, and it remains a practical everyday and meatless meal.
staple_dishes.significance: A familiar home dish whose preparation varies by region and family.

staple_dishes.name: Kibbeh and Kuba
staple_dishes.description: Ground meat combined with bulgur, rice, herbs, or spices and shaped or prepared in several regional forms.
staple_dishes.significance: Often associated with hospitality, celebrations, and collective preparation.

staple_dishes.name: Dolma
staple_dishes.description: Grape leaves and vegetables filled with rice, herbs, and sometimes meat. Ingredients and names differ across households.

staple_dishes.name: Tepsi and baked vegetable dishes
staple_dishes.description: Layered vegetables, meat, and sauce baked in a tray, with versions adapted to local ingredients and contemporary kitchens.

staple_dishes.name: Rice and wheat dishes
staple_dishes.description: Rice, bulgur, wheat berries, and noodles accompany stews and vegetables; recipes reflect both Mesopotamian and Levantine regional practices.

breads_and_grains.name: Flatbreads
breads_and_grains.description: Pita, thin breads, and locally available breads remain part of daily meals and shared hospitality.
breads_and_grains.significance: Bread connects household meals with regional and family practice.

breads_and_grains.name: Bulgur and wheat
breads_and_grains.description: Bulgur, freekeh, and other wheat products are used in pilafs, soups, salads, and meat dishes.
breads_and_grains.significance: These grains preserve a connection to older agricultural foodways while remaining adaptable.

breads_and_grains.name: Rice
breads_and_grains.description: Rice is prepared in plain, spiced, vegetable, and celebratory forms, especially in Mesopotamian family traditions.
breads_and_grains.significance: Rice dishes are commonly served at gatherings and life-cycle events.

preserved_foods.name: Pickled vegetables
preserved_foods.description: Turnips, cucumbers, peppers, eggplant, and olives are preserved in salt, vinegar, or brine.
preserved_foods.significance: Preserves extend seasonal food supplies and accompany daily meals.

preserved_foods.name: Dried herbs and fruit
preserved_foods.description: Herbs, grapes, figs, dates, and other produce may be dried for later use.
preserved_foods.significance: Drying remains a household practice where time and ingredients permit.

preserved_foods.name: Labneh and aged cheese
preserved_foods.description: Strained yogurt and brined or aged cheeses are served with bread and prepared foods.
preserved_foods.significance: Preserved dairy links everyday meals with regional food knowledge.

festive_dishes.name: Kleicha and Kulecheh
festive_dishes.description: Date- or nut-filled pastries prepared in some Christian households for Christmas, Easter, and family visits.
festive_dishes.significance: Preparation and distribution reinforce family and church-community ties.

festive_dishes.name: Ma'amoul and baklava
festive_dishes.description: Pastries and sweets served at religious holidays, weddings, and visits, with recipes differing by community.
festive_dishes.significance: Sweets mark hospitality and collective celebration.

festive_dishes.name: Celebration meals
festive_dishes.description: Rice, meat, stuffed vegetables, stews, breads, and salads may be prepared for weddings, baptisms, funerals, and community events.
festive_dishes.significance: Shared meals organize social support and public belonging.

beverages.name: Coffee
beverages.description: Coffee is prepared and served to guests in many homeland and diaspora households.
beverages.significance: Serving coffee expresses welcome and social reciprocity.

beverages.name: Tea
beverages.description: Black and herbal teas are common in homes and social gatherings, with regional preferences.
beverages.significance: Tea accompanies conversation and informal community life.

beverages.name: Yogurt drinks
beverages.description: Salted or mint-flavored yogurt drinks are served with meals, especially in warm weather.
beverages.significance: A practical drink associated with regional foodways.

regional_variations.characteristics: Levantine salads, breads, legumes, herbs, and vegetable dishes are common, with substantial local and family variation.
Rice, wheat, stews, stuffed vegetables, fish, and distinctive Assyrian or Chaldean family recipes are prominent in many households.
Breads, grains, dairy, preserved foods, and recipes shaped by southeastern Anatolian experience remain important.
Families combine inherited recipes with available ingredients, restaurant practices, and food traditions of their countries of residence.

cultural_significance.family_practice: Cooking is often a form of intergenerational teaching in which recipes, vocabulary, and memories are shared.
cultural_significance.diaspora_role: Food links diaspora families to relatives, places of origin, and community celebrations while allowing adaptation to new circumstances.
cultural_significance.community_centers: Churches, cultural associations, restaurants, and festivals can provide settings for shared meals and culinary teaching.
cultural_significance.cultural_bridge: Modern cuisine preserves continuity through practice rather than through one fixed or universally representative menu.
